results.cause: The deployment runs image "busybox:1.36" with command ["/app/payment-gateway","--listen=:8443"], but busybox does not contain that binary: "exec: \"/app/payment-gateway\": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory" (StartError, exit 128). The image is most likely wrong (a placeholder busybox instead of the payment-gateway app image), or the binary path is wrong. The rule finding mentions exit 127, but the actual exit code is 128 (StartError). The cause is the same: the command file is missing.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image in deployment/payment-gateway to the actual payment-gateway application image that contains /app/payment-gateway, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<your-payment-gateway-image>:<tag>
If the image is correct but the binary lives elsewhere, change the command in the container spec to the real binary path inside the image.
After the fix, the rollout starts a new ReplicaSet. Watch it with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/payment-gateway (the current rollout hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded).

results.cause: Migration 0042_add_orders_index tries to create an index that already exists: the log shows "ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists" and the script ends with exit 1. As written in the pod spec, the init container's args always echo that error and "exit 1", so it can never succeed. In a real migration this pattern means the migration is not idempotent, or the index was created earlier but the migration was not recorded as applied.
fix: Make the migration idempotent, e.g. use CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ..., or skip it when the relation already exists.
If orders_idx already exists from a partial or manual run, mark migration 0042_add_orders_index as applied in the migration tracking table, or drop orders_idx and let the migration recreate it.
Update the migrate init container's command/args in deployment/orders-api so it does not unconditionally `exit 1`, then roll out: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/orders-api

results.cause: The app rejects its config at startup: the fatal log line is "config: MAX_CONNECTIONS=\"ten\" is not an integer". MAX_CONNECTIONS is set to the word "ten" instead of a number, so the process exits 1. The redis:6379 and statsd:8125 "connection refused" errors are not the cause: the cache error falls back to in-memory, and the statsd error is logged after "shutting down".
fix: Set MAX_CONNECTIONS to an integer (e.g. "10") in the Deployment's container env, or in the ConfigMap/Secret it comes from: kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/pricing-api -c api MAX_CONNECTIONS=10
If the value comes from a ConfigMap/Secret, fix it there and restart: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/pricing-api
Separately, check that the redis service (CACHE_URL) and statsd:8125 (STATSD_ADDR) are reachable so the pod gets a shared cache and metrics, though neither causes the crash.

results.cause: The startup script requires DATABASE_URL and exits 1 when it is empty. The log says "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set", and the container env only defines DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL. There is no DATABASE_URL. Also, the script echoes the DB password to the logs (a password value was present and was redacted here).
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env in deployment/checkout-api, preferably via valueFrom.secretKeyRef since it likely contains credentials. Example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/checkout-api --from=secret/<db-secret> --keys=DATABASE_URL (or edit the manifest and kubectl apply).
Let the rollout create a new pod and confirm it stays Running: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api
Remove the line that echoes password=$DB_PASSWORD from the startup script so the credential is no longer written to logs, and consider rotating that password.

results.cause: DB_HOST is set to orders-db, and the startup script exits 1 when nslookup fails. The log shows "FATAL: db: dial tcp: lookup orders-db on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host". Cluster DNS answers but has no record for orders-db, so there is most likely no Service named orders-db in namespace pfa-lab, or it lives in another namespace and needs the qualified name orders-db.<namespace>.
fix: Check whether the Service exists: kubectl get svc orders-db -n pfa-lab. If it is missing, deploy the Postgres workload and its Service named orders-db in pfa-lab.

If the database runs in another namespace or under a different Service name, set DB_HOST in the deployment's container env to the correct name (e.g. orders-db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local), e.g. kubectl set env deployment/shipping-api -n pfa-lab DB_HOST=<correct-host>.
Once the name resolves, the pod recovers on its next restart, or you can force it with kubectl rollout restart deployment/shipping-api -n pfa-lab.

results.cause: api: the startup script exits 1 with "FATAL: required environment variable REDIS_URL is not set"; the container only has env var PORT (env_names: ["PORT"]). worker: the script exits 2 with "error: open /etc/cart/worker.yaml: no such file or directory"; its only mount is /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount, so nothing provides /etc/cart/worker.yaml.
fix: api: add REDIS_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env in deployment/cart-service. If it holds credentials, use valueFrom.secretKeyRef pointing to a Secret.

worker: create a ConfigMap with key worker.yaml (e.g. kubectl create configmap cart-worker-config -n pfa-lab --from-file=worker.yaml). Add it as a volume in the pod spec and mount it in containers[name=worker].volumeMounts at mountPath /etc/cart.
Apply the changes and watch the rollout: kubectl rollout status deployment/cart-service -n pfa-lab

results.cause: The registry answers "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found" (rpc error code = NotFound). The tag "1.36.1-uclbic" looks like a typo of the busybox libc variant "uclibc" ("uclbic" has the letters swapped), so the reference points to a tag that does not exist. This is not a credentials or network problem.
fix: Correct the image tag on the container, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc`, or edit spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image in the manifest and re-apply.
Confirm the tag exists before rolling out: `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` or `crane ls busybox`.
Watch the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront`. The new ReplicaSet will replace the stuck pod.

results.cause: The image field has two tags: "busybox:1.36:latest". A reference allows only one :tag, so the kubelet rejects it with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). This is a syntax error in the manifest, not a registry or credentials problem.
fix: Set the container image to a single tag, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36`, or change `spec.template.spec.containers[name=worker].image` in the manifest to `busybox:1.36`.
If the image is built from templated values (e.g. repo:tag plus an appended :latest), fix the template so only one tag is added.
The Deployment reports ProgressDeadlineExceeded. After you fix the image, confirm the new rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/notify-worker`.

results.cause: The registry answered NotFound: "docker.io/library/busybox:1.63: not found". The tag "1.63" does not exist for the official busybox repository, so the tag is wrong or a typo. Separately, the pull secret "regcred" is missing ("Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (regcred)"). That is not the cause here: busybox is a public image and the registry returned "not found", not "unauthorized".
fix: Change the container image in deployment/admin-portal (spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image) to an existing busybox tag, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/admin-portal web=busybox:<valid-tag>`. Confirm the tag exists first with `crane ls busybox` or `docker manifest inspect busybox:<tag>`.
Watch the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/admin-portal`.
Fix the missing pull secret: remove `regcred` from spec.template.spec.imagePullSecrets (busybox is public), or create the secret `regcred` in namespace pfa-lab if a private registry is intended.

results.cause: The node pulls through the registry mirror registry-mirror:1273, which returned "500 Internal Server Error" for the HEAD request to /v2/billing/ui/manifests/3.2.0?ns=registry.pfa-lab.invalid. The mirror could not fetch the image from the upstream registry. The hostname registry.pfa-lab.invalid uses the reserved .invalid TLD, which never resolves, so the image reference most likely points at a wrong or nonexistent registry. Less likely, the mirror itself is broken.
fix: Correct the registry hostname in the Deployment's spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image to the real registry that hosts billing/ui:3.2.0, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<correct-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0`.
If registry.pfa-lab.invalid is intentional, make sure the mirror registry-mirror:1273 has a working upstream configured for that registry, and check the mirror's logs for the 500 error.
After the pull succeeds, confirm the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/billing-ui`.

results.cause: The container command runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0`, which allocates 300M (log: "cache warmup: loading remaining 100MB"). The container limit is resources.limits.memory: 200Mi, so the kernel kills it each time (reason OOMKilled, exit code 137). The workload needs at least ~300M plus overhead, which a 200Mi limit cannot hold.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) on container cache in statefulset/session-cache above the 300M working set, e.g. to 384Mi, or 448Mi for headroom as the rule finding suggests. Example: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"384Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"384Mi"}]'
Or keep the 200Mi limit and lower the load: change the args to `--vm-bytes` below ~180M (e.g. 150M) so the process fits within the limit.
If the pod is not recreated automatically, run kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pod session-cache-0 so the StatefulSet recreates it with the new spec.

results.cause: The container runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0` and logs "loading 250MB of order history into memory", but resources.limits.memory is 128Mi. 250M is about 238Mi, nearly double the limit, so it is OOMKilled (exit code 137) within the same second it starts (started/finished 14:54:50).
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory on container worker to at least 320Mi (250M is about 238Mi, plus runtime overhead), e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=320Mi --requests=memory=256Mi`.
Alternatively, reduce what the job loads at once (batch or stream the order history, or lower --vm-bytes) so peak usage stays below 128Mi.
After the change, confirm the new pod reaches Ready and check actual usage with `kubectl -n pfa-lab top pod`.

results.cause: The container command runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0`, which allocates and holds 200M of memory (log line: "log-shipper starting, buffering 200MB of logs in memory"). The container limit is only `limits.memory: 64Mi`, so the kernel OOM-kills it at once (last state OOMKilled, exit code 137, started and finished at 14:54:20). The 128Mi example in the rule finding is too low, because the configured allocation is 200M.
fix: Raise the log-shipper memory to cover the 200M allocation plus headroom: set resources.limits.memory and resources.requests.memory to 256Mi in deployment/search-api (e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi`).
Or keep the 64Mi limit and lower the in-memory buffer: change `--vm-bytes 200M` to a value well under 64Mi (e.g. 32M), or configure the real log shipper to buffer less in memory or spill to disk.
Watch the pod after the change: `kubectl -n pfa-lab get pod -w` should show log-shipper Ready with no new OOMKilled restarts.

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores), which is almost certainly a unit typo for "4000m" (4 cores). The scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu" and "Preemption is not helpful for scheduling" because no node offers anywhere near 4000 cores.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu from "4k"/"4000" to "4000m", or lower it to what the trainer actually needs, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m
Keep the request at or below the node's allocatable CPU (check with kubectl describe node). If even 4 cores exceeds it, lower the request further or add a larger node.
After the rollout, confirm the new pod schedules: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ml-trainer

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab: "MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume \"templates\" : configmap \"email-templates\" not found" (x1075 since 2026-11-02T15:26:39). The Deployment has since hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the right namespace, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>`. The kubelet retries the mount and the pod will start.
If the configmap exists under another name, fix spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.name in deployment/email-sender to match it.
If the templates are optional, set spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.optional: true so the pod can start without them.
After the fix, check rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/email-sender`. Use `kubectl rollout restart` if needed, since the deployment reported ProgressDeadlineExceeded.

results.cause: The pod spec sets nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, but the only node in the cluster does not carry that label: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". Preemption cannot help ("Preemption is not helpful for scheduling"), so the pod will never schedule as configured.
fix: If the workload doesn't actually need an A100 node (it runs busybox:1.36 with `sleep 3600`), remove the selector: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
Otherwise, check node labels with `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` and set spec.template.spec.nodeSelector to a label that actually exists on the intended node.
If the existing node is the intended GPU node, label it: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
If a GPU A100 node is genuinely required, add one with label hardware=gpu-a100 to the cluster.

results.cause: PVC metrics-data requests storageClassName "fast-ssd", which does not exist in the cluster (ProvisioningFailed x102: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found). No volume is provisioned, so the scheduler reports "pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims" and the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Run `kubectl get storageclass` to see which StorageClasses exist (note the default one).

Delete and recreate PVC metrics-data in namespace pfa-lab with spec.storageClassName set to an existing class, or omit it to use the default (storageClassName is immutable on an existing claim): `kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pvc metrics-data`, then re-apply the manifest with the corrected class.
Alternatively, have a cluster admin create a StorageClass named fast-ssd with a working provisioner, and the existing claim will bind.
After the claim is Bound, the pod schedules automatically. If the Deployment stays stuck, run `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/metrics-store`.

results.cause: The readiness check depends on the database host in DB_HOST, and that hostname does not resolve. The logs repeat "readiness: database inventory-db:5432 unreachable: lookup inventory-db: no such host". The probe itself is correct: port http=80 and path /cgi-bin/ready match what the app serves ("listening on :80"). The app is deliberately reporting 503 because its dependency is missing. Most likely there is no Service named inventory-db in namespace pfa-lab, or the database lives in another namespace and needs a qualified name.
fix: Create the missing inventory-db Service in pfa-lab, or deploy the database it should front. Confirm with: kubectl get svc inventory-db -n pfa-lab

If the database runs in another namespace, set the DB_HOST env var on container api to inventory-db.<namespace> (or the correct Service name). For example: kubectl set env deployment/stock-api -n pfa-lab DB_HOST=inventory-db.<namespace>
Leave the readiness probe unchanged. It is correctly keeping traffic away until the database resolves. Once DB_HOST resolves, the pod becomes Ready without a restart.

results.cause: The readiness probe is configured as "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves /healthz: the startup command creates /www/healthz and the log says "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz". httpd returns 404 for /ready (event: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404", x44263). The port is correct (http=80/TCP, httpd -p 80); only the path is wrong.
fix: Change spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path from /ready to /healthz in deployment/catalog-api, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]'
Alternatively, make the app serve /ready (e.g. add 'echo ok > /www/ready' to the container args) if /ready is the intended endpoint.
After the rollout, verify with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/catalog-api.

results.cause: The app deliberately sleeps 45 seconds (log: "ledger-api replaying journal, this takes about 45 seconds") before starting httpd on port 80. The liveness probe starts after initialDelaySeconds=2, runs every periodSeconds=3 with failureThreshold=2, and there is no startupProbe. The container is killed a few seconds after start with "connect: connection refused" on :80, ending with exit code 137. The "listening on :80" line never appears in the logs. The port matches (http=80), so startup timing is the problem.
fix: Add a startupProbe to container api: httpGet path /healthz port http, periodSeconds 5, failureThreshold 18 (allows ~90s). The liveness probe only begins once startup succeeds.
Alternatively, raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to at least 60 (above the 45s replay plus margin) and consider failureThreshold 3+.
Optionally add a readinessProbe on /healthz port http so traffic only arrives once the app is serving.

results.cause: The liveness probe is configured as "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80 -h /www", logs "inventory-api listening on :80" and the container declares only http=80/TCP. Every probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused", and after failure_threshold 2 the container is killed (last state exit code 137, reason Error).
fix: In the StatefulSet inventory-api, change containers[api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port from 8080 to 80 (or to the named port "http").

Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]', then delete pod inventory-api-0 if it does not roll automatically.
Optionally relax the probe (e.g. timeout_seconds > 1, failure_threshold > 2) to avoid restarts on transient slowness.
